thread.document:
The optimizers part of the course (lectures 2-7) can feel very heavy and overwhelming. I find it useful to try and condense information as much as possible so I can focus on the right things. Often times such condensed information comes in the form of a cheat sheet. Although these are not allowed for the final, I find it useful for studying.

Here were the steps I did:



Step 1 — Compress the slides

I asked the AI to turn the slide content into a very concise, high-yield cheat sheet:

keep only essential concepts

remove redundancy

keep key equations + intuition

organize clearly

one-page style

This helped turn dense content into something readable.



Step 2 — Let the AI self-critique

Next, I asked the AI to review and correct its own summary:

fix inaccuracies

add missing assumptions

clean notation

group related topics

add a short “unifying principles” section

Repeating this step improves both accuracy and clarity.



Step 3 — Generate questions to find my gaps

Then I asked the AI to create diagnostic questions to test deeper understanding:

NTK vs feature learning

width scaling + μP

gradient/curvature effects

what momentum can/can’t fix

how Muon differs from true second-order methods

I answered the questions myself, and the AI pointed out gaps + updated the cheat sheet.

This made the notes personalized to my actual misunderstandings. Once again, this can be done repeatedly to keep refining the cheat sheet.



Step 4 — Convert to LaTeX (optional)

Once everything was refined, I had the AI output a LaTeX version so it looks clean for studying.
